fields.content:
NOAA’s GOES-U Satellite: One Year Later
Publication date: 2025-06-25

On June 25, 2024, GOES-U, the final satellite in NOAA’s GOES-R Series, launched from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Once GOES-U [reached geostationary orbit](https://www.nesdis.noaa.gov/news/noaas-goes-u-reaches-geostationary-orbit-now-designated-goes-19) on July 7, the satellite was renamed GOES-19. As NOAA marks the first anniversary of sending GOES-U into space, we check in with the newest satellite in NOAA’s fleet.

NOAA’s GOES-U Reaches Geostationary Orbit, Now Designated GOES-19
Publication date: 2024-07-08

On July 7, 2024, NOAA's GOES-U satellite reached geostationary orbit above Earth's equator and was renamed GOES-19.

On July 7, 2024, NOAA’s GOES-U executed its final engine burn, placing the satellite in geostationary orbit 22,236 miles above Earth’s equator. Upon reaching this milestone, GOES-U was renamed GOES-19. GOES satellites are designated with a letter prior to launch and a number once they achieve geostationary orbit.
